entries.description: Delete the inferred import graph and everything that serves it: `PACKAGE`, `module_name_for`, `_imports_in`, `build_import_graph`, `_closure`, `build_test_dependencies`, and the `dependency-edge` and `module-ownership` reasons. The reasons that remain — `changed-test`, `configured-rule`, `repo_wide`, and smoke on `selection_unknown` — carry no language knowledge.

Replace `test_*.py` discovery with declared test roots and a declared test-file glob, so a repository states where its tests live and what they are called instead of the framework guessing a pytest convention.

Declare this repository's own mapping under `testing.selection.rules`, covering what the graph used to infer. Rules are the honest form of a mapping that was always a guess; where a module genuinely affects many suites, say so.
Affected tests, recorded as the `preverify-targeted` evidence.
Cross-provider verification; then the full suite once, against the final verified tree.

Deleted the AST import graph from affected.py: PACKAGE, module_name_for, _imports_in, build_import_graph, _closure, build_test_dependencies, test_files, and the module-ownership and dependency-edge reasons. Remaining reasons carry no language knowledge.
Replaced tree discovery of test_*.py with declared testing.selection.test_roots plus a declared test_glob, matched case-sensitively against the file name and confirmed present in the tree.
Declared one testing.selection rule per ai_router module, naming the tests that would notice it breaking, replacing what the import graph inferred.
Ran the selector's targeted command (103 tests, green) and recorded it as preverify-targeted evidence; accepted under the targeted policy.

Round 1 ISSUES_FOUND (evidence.py and ledger.py rules omitted tests/test_critique_contracts.py, which imports both); remediated, reran the fix's targeted tests, round 2 VERIFIED by gpt-5.5/openai over copilot-cli.
